newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF EASILY BEATS RUBIN TO ADVANCE IN PHILDELPHIA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF EASILY BEATS RUBIN TO ADVANCE IN PHILDELPHIA.

text.p: Steffi Graf unleashed an
impressive performance in a 6-0, 6-3 victory over Chanda Rubin
Friday night in the quarterfinals of the $450,000 Advanta
Championships Friday.
Graf, the top seed and defending champion, will face
unseeded American Marianne Werdel Witmeyer, a 6-2 6-3 winner
over Barbara Paulus of Austria, in Saturday's semifinals.
In other quarterfinal matches Friday, third-seed Jana
Novotna used a variety of shots and approaches to blunt
hard-hitting American Anne Miller 6-3 6-0. Novotna's opponent
in Saturday's semifinals will be Yayuk Basuki, who defeated
local product Lisa Raymond 5-7 6-3 6-3.
Earlier Friday, Graf's father, Peter, was released from
jail in Mannheim, Germany, where he had been held for the last
15 months on charges of tax evasion.
"Obviously I'm very happy for my father and my family,"
Graf said Friday. "I wish I could have been home, but I have
two more weeks of tennis."
Graf said she would return to Germany after playing in
next week's year-ending WTA Tour championships, where she is
also the defending champion.
Against Rubin, Graf sailed through the first set in 19
minutes and didn't allow Rubin a game-point opportunity until
the fourth game of the second set. Rubin held serve for the
first time in the match to win that game, but couldn't manage
a break point on Graf's serve the rest of the match.
Graf said she wasn't surprised she was able to play so
well after a long layoff. She had played in only one
tournament since the U.S. Open due to a left knee injury.
"I've done it so many times," she said, "but I'm still
impressed I can do it."
The veteran Novotna dropped the first three games to
Miller before winning the next 12 games in a row, negating the
19-year-old's power from the baseline by utilizing her
customary slices, drop shots and net approaches.
Miller appeared to have Novotna broken in the fifth game
of the second set, but Novotna's double-fault was overruled by
the chair umpire. Visibly affected, Miller hit her next two
returns out, and Novotna went on to hold serve and then won
the match a game later.
After losing a 58-minute first set to Raymond, the
33rd-ranked Basuki didn't lose a service game the rest of the
match, and used early service breaks in the second and third
sets to move into her third semifinal of the year.
